feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A vow is a spoken or written act, not a material artifact.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — It is a culturally invented form of speech with defined purpose.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Requires no energy source beyond human expression.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not physically load-bearing or architecturally relevant.
feedback.Observable: Included — Delivered audibly and visibly, often in ceremonial contexts.
feedback.Physical Medium: Included — Performed via the human voice and body; dependent on physical sound transmission.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires human agents to initiate; not autonomous.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Composed intentionally to declare and formalize commitment.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Included — Performs a speech act with social and legal consequences (e.g., changes marital status).
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Does not perform logic or transformation of data.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Symbolizes transformation, but does not modify internal state independently.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Delivered to and often reciprocated by another person.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Legally significant, but not a subsystem within a technical structure.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Requires contextual and human execution.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Vows are traditional but not strictly required in all legal marriages.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Represents union, loyalty, duty, and future intent.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Communicates emotional and legal intent to witnesses and institutions.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Typically follows formal structures, religious or civil formats.
feedback.Compositional: Excluded — Often delivered as a coherent whole rather than modular parts.
feedback.Normative: Included — Encodes expected behaviors in marriage (fidelity, support, etc.).
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not reference itself or abstract categories.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Performed at a defined time with reference to future duration.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Excluded — Exists in speech, not virtual or simulated format.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists only through shared understanding and social ceremony.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Required by some legal or religious marriage frameworks.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Formally binds personal and social identity into a new status (spouse).
feedback.Regulated: Included — In some jurisdictions, specific language or presence of vows is legally required.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Triggers a change in legal and financial obligations (e.g., shared assets).
feedback.Politicised: Excluded — Marriage may be politicised, but the vow itself is not inherently contested.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Central to wedding ceremonies; highly choreographed and culturally patterned.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Enacts moral promises, tied to duty, love, and personal integrity.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the wedding vow as a performative speech act — embodied, intentional, and socially consequential. It is symbolic, rule-based, economically and ethically significant, and delivered within regulated, ritualized contexts. Its abstract, physical, and social properties are all essential to its identity.
